name: PostGate – Paywall, Content Monetization & Stripe Subscriptions
author: QodeSphere

sections.description:
WordPress Paywall Plugin for Paid Content and Stripe Subscriptions

PostGate is a WordPress paywall and content monetization plugin for creators, bloggers, educators, consultants, and publishers who want to sell premium content directly from their own website.

Create a paywall for an entire site, category, taxonomy, post, page, custom post type, or selected content blocks. Sell individual articles with one-time payments, offer recurring subscriptions, or display both options on the same paywall. Stripe-hosted checkout handles payments while PostGate manages content access inside WordPress.

PostGate gives you the paid-content and content-restriction features needed to generate revenue without configuring a complete e-commerce store or a complex traditional membership plugin.

  • PostGate Documentation
  • Quick Start Guide
  • WordPress.org Support Forum

Monetize Content Directly from WordPress

Turn articles, resources, and subscriber-only sections into a paid content business while keeping ownership of your website, audience, and publishing workflow.

With PostGate, you can:

  • Add a WordPress paywall without installing a full e-commerce platform.
  • Sell paid articles, tutorials, reports, and other premium content.
  • Accept one-time payments for individual content access.
  • Create recurring content subscriptions with Stripe.
  • Combine one-time purchases and subscription options on the same paywall.
  • Require free registration or login without requiring a payment.
  • Manage purchases, subscriptions, and access from WordPress.
  • Keep a public content preview visible before the paywall.

Whether you want to monetize a single premium article or build a subscription-based publication, PostGate lets you choose how each part of your content is sold.

Built for Creators, Bloggers, Educators, and Publishers

PostGate is designed for people and organizations that publish valuable content:

  • Content creators: Sell exclusive articles and subscriber-only resources.
  • Bloggers: Add a paywall to premium posts while keeping other articles free.
  • News and niche publishers: Build a paid publication with article purchases or recurring subscriptions.
  • Educators and instructors: Restrict tutorials, lessons, and educational resources.
  • Consultants and coaches: Monetize professional advice, reports, and private content.
  • Researchers and analysts: Sell access to research, case studies, and industry insights.
  • Membership-style websites: Offer subscription-based content access without a complex community system.

Popular WordPress Paywall Use Cases

PostGate can support different paid-content strategies:

  • Sell content on WordPress without adding a shopping cart.
  • Sell a single premium article with a one-time payment.
  • Offer monthly or annual access to a premium blog.
  • Protect every post in a paid category or taxonomy.
  • Create a full-site paywall for a subscriber publication.
  • Keep an introduction free and lock the remaining Gutenberg blocks.
  • Require user registration for selected content without charging a fee.
  • Offer both pay-per-article and recurring subscription options.
  • Use different products and prices for different posts, pages, or content collections.

Flexible WordPress Paywall and Content Restriction

PostGate combines paywall payments with granular content restriction. Restrict content with broad access rules, then override them for a specific category, post, page, or block when needed.

  • Site-wide paywall: Protect the entire WordPress website with a payment, active subscription, or login requirement.
  • Post-type restriction: Enable content protection for posts, pages, and supported custom post types.
  • Category and taxonomy restriction: Monetize a collection of related content with one access rule.
  • Post and page paywall: Sell access to an individual article, page, tutorial, report, or resource.
  • Block-level content restriction: Use the PostGate Lock Block to protect selected Gutenberg blocks while leaving the rest of the page public.
  • Login-only content: Restrict content to registered and logged-in WordPress users without charging them.
  • Role-based access: Allow administrators, editors, or selected custom roles to bypass a paywall.
  • Granular overrides: Let post-level rules override category or site-wide content restriction settings.

This flexible access system supports both simple paid content and membership-style content access without forcing every page into the same plan.

Sell Paid Content with One-Time Purchases

Use one-time Stripe payments when visitors should pay once to unlock specific premium content.

One-time purchases work well for:

  • Paid articles and investigative reports
  • Pay-per-post and article paywall access
  • Premium tutorials and how-to guides
  • Research papers, whitepapers, and case studies
  • Educational resources and individual lessons
  • Industry analysis and professional insights
  • Exclusive posts and content archives

Assign different Stripe products and prices to different content. Visitors can choose an available product, complete Stripe Checkout, and return to the protected page with access after the successful payment is confirmed.

Create Recurring Content Subscriptions

Use recurring Stripe prices to sell monthly, annual, or custom-interval content subscriptions. Subscribers can receive ongoing access to a category, collection, individual post, or the entire website according to your paywall rules.

As a paid content and subscription plugin, PostGate lets you:

  • Offer recurring subscriptions for premium content.
  • Build a subscriber-only publication or knowledge hub.
  • Combine subscription access with individual paid articles.
  • Display multiple subscription products or pricing choices.
  • Grant access after a successful subscription checkout.
  • Revoke subscription-based access after cancellation.

PostGate supports membership-style subscriptions focused on protected content. It is a simpler alternative when you do not need community profiles, member directories, or the additional administration of a full membership platform.

Stripe Payments and Automatic Content Access

Connect a Stripe account through OAuth, synchronize products and prices, and use Stripe-hosted checkout for paywall payments. This creates a Stripe paywall without collecting card details on your WordPress server.

Stripe and payment features include:

  • Stripe Connect account connection
  • Stripe-hosted Checkout
  • One-time prices and recurring subscription prices
  • Multiple products and pricing choices
  • Sandbox and live payment modes
  • Verified Stripe webhook processing
  • Automatic access after successful payment
  • Automatic subscription access revocation after cancellation
  • Refund-related access updates for supported webhook events
  • Currencies and payment methods available to the connected Stripe account

Available payment methods, currencies, processing fees, and Stripe Connect capabilities depend on the connected account’s country, business type, and Stripe configuration.

SEO-Friendly Paywall and Content Previews

PostGate can keep an introduction public while protecting the premium section of a post or page. Choose a preview based on a number of paragraphs or words, then customize the limit globally or for individual content.

A useful public preview can:

  • Give search engines indexable context about the page.
  • Help visitors understand the value of the premium content.
  • Preserve a shareable introduction before the paywall.
  • Encourage readers to purchase an article or start a subscription.

The preview is not a promise of search rankings. For the best reader and search experience, publish an accurate teaser that genuinely describes the protected content.

Email Notifications for Orders and Subscriber Updates

PostGate includes configurable email notifications to keep customers and subscribers informed without extra plugins.

Email notification features include:

  • Customer order notifications after successful purchases.
  • Manual-order email notifications with configurable subject and message.
  • Subscriber content-update notifications when new protected content is published.
  • Batch processing for large subscriber lists to reduce performance impact.
  • Configurable sender name, sender email, and HTML email support.

Use these notifications to improve post-purchase communication and keep active subscribers aware of new premium content.

Stripe Billing Portal for Subscription Self-Service

PostGate includes Stripe Billing Portal access so subscribers can manage billing details and subscriptions through Stripe’s secure hosted interface.

Stripe Billing Portal features include:

  • Open portal links from Subscription Manager and account/profile flows.
  • Update payment methods and billing information in Stripe.
  • Download invoices and billing history from Stripe.
  • Cancel subscriptions directly in the portal according to your Stripe setup.
  • Safe return URLs and authenticated session handling for portal redirects.

This gives subscribers self-service billing management while keeping card and billing operations in Stripe.

Gutenberg and WordPress-Native Paywall Controls

PostGate works inside familiar WordPress publishing workflows:

  • Native paywall controls in the Block Editor sidebar
  • Gutenberg Lock Block for block-level content restriction
  • Settings for global, post-type, category, taxonomy, post, and page access
  • WordPress user accounts for purchase and subscription access
  • WordPress role bypass rules
  • Translation-ready and RTL-ready interface

Post and page restrictions can work with page builders that render content through standard WordPress content filters. The PostGate Lock Block requires the WordPress Block Editor. Test the complete checkout and access flow with your active theme, page builder, and caching configuration before launch.

Customizable WordPress Paywall Templates

Choose the paywall design and message that fit your content:

  • Compact responsive paywall template
  • Classic paywall template with product and pricing details
  • Custom badge, heading, description, and button text
  • Login and registration messages
  • Paragraph or word-count preview limits
  • Custom HTML before and after product options
  • Theme template overrides for advanced design changes
  • Post-purchase redirect behavior

The built-in layouts are mobile friendly, and developers can override PostGate templates in a theme for deeper customization.

Paid Content Orders, Revenue, and Access Management

PostGate provides WordPress administration tools for the paid-content workflow:

  • View one-time purchases and subscription orders.
  • Review payment and order status.
  • Track paywall revenue from the dashboard.
  • See which users received access to protected content.
  • Manage access grants when manual intervention is required.
  • Review Stripe webhook processing for payment and subscription events.

These tools keep content access and order information close to the WordPress posts and pages being monetized.

Developer-Friendly Content Monetization

Developers can extend and integrate the PostGate paywall through:

  • Theme template overrides
  • WordPress actions and filters
  • REST API endpoints
  • Custom post type and taxonomy support
  • Role and capability checks
  • A modern React-powered administration interface

PostGate follows WordPress development practices for sanitization, validation, nonces, roles, capabilities, internationalization, and extensibility.

How PostGate Works

  1. Install and activate the PostGate WordPress paywall plugin.
  2. Connect your Stripe account in Sandbox mode.
  3. Configure the Stripe webhook endpoint displayed by PostGate.
  4. Create one-time or recurring prices in Stripe and sync the products.
  5. Choose the site, category, taxonomy, post, page, or blocks to protect.
  6. Assign one or more products and configure the public content preview.
  7. Complete a test purchase and confirm that content access is granted.
  8. Switch PostGate and Stripe to live mode when the paywall is ready.

Documentation and Support

  • Read the PostGate Quick Start Guide
  • Browse PostGate Documentation
  • Ask for help in the WordPress.org Support Forum

External Services

PostGate connects to Stripe when an administrator connects an account, synchronizes products, creates a Checkout Session, or processes payment, refund, and subscription events. Stripe receives the account, product, price, customer, and transaction data needed for the requested operation. Stripe is required for paid-content features; login-only content restriction does not require a payment.

PostGate also communicates with a connection service operated by QodeSphere to initiate and complete the Stripe Connect OAuth flow. During this administrator-initiated connection, the site URL and Stripe authorization data needed to return the connection to WordPress may be transmitted. This service is used only when an administrator chooses to connect a Stripe account.

  • Stripe Services Agreement
  • Stripe Connected Account Agreement
  • Stripe Privacy Policy
  • PostGate Documentation
sections.installation:
Automatic Installation

  1. In the WordPress dashboard, go to Plugins > Add Plugin.
  2. Search for “PostGate”.
  3. Select Install Now, then Activate.
  4. Go to PostGate > Settings.

Manual Installation

  1. Download the PostGate ZIP file.
  2. In WordPress, go to Plugins > Add Plugin > Upload Plugin.
  3. Upload the ZIP file and select Install Now.
  4. Activate PostGate and go to PostGate > Settings.

Configure Your First WordPress Paywall

  1. Confirm that the website uses HTTPS and that WordPress user registration is enabled.
  2. Open PostGate > Settings > Payments and connect Stripe in Sandbox mode.
  3. Add the displayed webhook endpoint in Stripe and save the signing secret in PostGate.
  4. Create one-time or recurring prices in Stripe, then fetch and sync the products.
  5. Choose global or post-type content restriction settings, if needed.
  6. Edit a post or page, enable PostGate in the editor sidebar, and assign a product.
  7. Choose a paragraph or word-count preview and customize the paywall message.
  8. Complete a test purchase before switching PostGate and Stripe to live mode.
sections.faq:
What is a WordPress paywall plugin?

A WordPress paywall plugin restricts access to selected content until a visitor meets a requirement such as logging in, making a one-time purchase, or having an active subscription. PostGate supports each of these access models.

How do I add a paywall to WordPress?

Install PostGate, connect Stripe, configure the webhook, sync a product, and choose the content to protect. You can add a paywall to the entire site, a post type, category, taxonomy, individual post or page, or selected Gutenberg blocks.

How can I monetize or sell content on WordPress?

PostGate lets you monetize and sell content on WordPress through individual article payments, recurring subscriptions, or both options on the same paywall. You can also restrict content to logged-in users without requiring payment.

Can I sell paid articles and individual posts?

Yes. Assign a one-time Stripe price to a post or page to sell it individually. After Stripe confirms the payment, PostGate grants the WordPress user access to the paid content.

Can I use PostGate as a pay-per-post plugin?

Yes. PostGate supports a pay-per-post model by assigning a one-time Stripe price to an individual post or page. You can also offer a recurring subscription as an alternative to purchasing that article separately.

Can I offer both one-time payments and recurring subscriptions?

Yes. A paywall can display one-time purchase options, recurring subscription options, or both. Products and billing intervals are configured in Stripe and synchronized with PostGate.

Is PostGate a WordPress membership plugin?

PostGate supports recurring subscriptions, login-only content, role-based access, and membership-style content protection. Its primary focus is paywalls and paid content rather than member directories, social communities, profiles, or other features found in a complete membership plugin.

Can I create a membership website with PostGate?

You can create a subscription-based website where registered users pay for access to protected content. If your membership website mainly needs paid articles, premium categories, or full-site subscription access, PostGate may provide a simpler setup than a traditional membership platform.

What content can I restrict?

PostGate can restrict content across an entire site, supported post types, posts, pages, categories, taxonomies, and individual Gutenberg blocks. Post-level rules can override broader site-wide or category content restriction.

Can I lock only part of a post or page?

Yes. Add the PostGate Lock Block in the WordPress Block Editor and place the protected blocks inside it. Content outside the Lock Block remains public.

Is the PostGate paywall SEO friendly?

PostGate can show an indexable preview based on a selected number of paragraphs or words while the premium content remains protected. No paywall plugin can guarantee rankings, so the public teaser should be useful, descriptive, and consistent with what readers receive after purchase.

Does PostGate work with Gutenberg and page builders?

PostGate includes native Gutenberg sidebar controls and a Lock Block for block-level paywalls. Post and page restrictions can work with builders such as Elementor, Divi, and Beaver Builder when they use standard WordPress content rendering. Test your theme and page builder before accepting live payments.

Do customers need a WordPress account?

Yes. A customer must register or log in so PostGate can associate the purchase or subscription with the correct WordPress user and restore access on future visits.

Do I need a Stripe account?

Stripe is required for paid-content purchases and subscriptions. Login-only content restriction can be used without a payment. Stripe availability and Connect capabilities vary by country.

Which Stripe payment methods and currencies are supported?

PostGate uses the payment methods and currencies available to the connected Stripe account and selected Stripe Checkout configuration. Availability depends on the account country, business type, currency, and capabilities.

Can I test Stripe payments before launching the paywall?

Yes. Use PostGate and Stripe Sandbox mode to test products, Checkout, webhooks, purchases, subscriptions, and content access without processing live payments.

How much does PostGate cost?

PostGate is free to download and install from WordPress.org. A 5% PostGate platform fee applies to successful transactions, in addition to Stripe processing fees. Stripe fees depend on the connected account and country.

What happens when a subscription is canceled?

Stripe sends a supported webhook event to PostGate. PostGate then revokes the access associated with the canceled subscription according to the recorded order and content rules.

What happens when a payment is refunded?

For supported Stripe refund events, PostGate updates the related order and revokes the content access associated with the refunded payment.

Can I customize the WordPress paywall design?

Yes. Choose a Compact or Classic template, customize the badge, heading, description, buttons, login message, and surrounding HTML, or override PostGate templates in your theme.

Does PostGate work with WordPress caching plugins?

It can, but logged-in and personalized paid-content pages should not be served from a shared public cache. Confirm that your caching plugin excludes logged-in users and test purchase, login, cancellation, and access flows before launch.

Do I need WooCommerce or another e-commerce plugin?

No. PostGate connects directly to Stripe and is designed to sell access to WordPress content without requiring WooCommerce or a separate shopping-cart plugin.
